title: CFC-11 narrows steady-transport fits on P02 but permits the central density 26.5 fit at five percent error
abstract: We test whether a third measured gas resolves a two-gas ambiguity in North Pacific oxygen loss. We fit repeated P02 gas means with any nonnegative, unchanged transit-age distribution under fixed full source saturation and sample-based partial-pressure normalization. At 28-32 N, 180-160 W, density 26.5 AOU rose 8.36 micromol/kg from 2013 to 2022. Adding CFC-11 raises the minimum tracer error allowance from 1.10 to 4.85 percent; adding 2004 gives 4.96 percent. Thus steady transport still fits within five percent, despite the oxygen loss. Two- and six-degree bins also permit this central fit. In the west, all five density classes from 26.3 to 26.7 fail the three-epoch test at five percent, but need only 5.20-6.30 percent. Western 2022 CFC-11 is below its allowed omitted-observation prediction. Sampling ranges and source-factor tests limit interpretation: central 26.5 two-epoch error spans 2.36-8.73 percent across spatial resamples, and a 2.5 percent CFC-11 source-factor change reverses its three-epoch pass. Code, source hashes, aggregate observations, positive fits and dual evidence are included. These conditional gas constraints do not attribute oxygen loss to ventilation, respiration or outcrop change.
